codeReview.summary: lib/factory-accounts.js correctly implements all 9 required functions following the codex-accounts.js pattern. The module properly loads Factory accounts from three sources (env var, container file, auth.v2 fallback) with priority ordering and deduplication by accountId. JWT profile extraction handles WorkOS-specific claims (email, org_id, sub, first_name+last_name). All functions have proper JSDoc documentation, error handling (returning empty arrays on failure), and use the established section divider convention. Barrel re-exports are correctly added to shuvquota.js. Tests are comprehensive (51 tests) covering happy paths, error cases (missing files, malformed JSON, empty env, corrupt auth, missing JWT claims), deduplication, and edge cases.

issues.description: isValidFactoryAccount only checks for label+accountId, unlike Codex's isValidAccount which also requires access+refresh tokens. This is a reasonable design choice since Factory accounts from the container file may not carry tokens, but downstream modules (factory-usage.js, factory-tokens.js) will need to handle accounts that pass validation but lack tokens for API calls.

loadFactoryAccountFromAuthV2 stores tokens as accessToken/refreshToken (camelCase) while Codex uses access/refresh. This is consistent with readAuthV2Files output but differs from the Codex convention. The future factory-tokens.js module and FACTORY_TOKEN_FIELDS field map (referenced in architecture.md) will need to account for this naming difference.

loadAllFactoryAccounts reads from a single file path (FACTORY_MULTI_ACCOUNT_PATH) unlike Codex which iterates over MULTI_ACCOUNT_PATHS array. This matches the feature spec which only mentions ~/.factory-accounts.json, but if multi-path support is needed later, the function signature would need changing.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The Factory accounts module uses camelCase token fields (accessToken/refreshToken) while the Codex module uses shorthand (access/refresh). This naming difference is not documented in AGENTS.md or architecture.md. Future workers building factory-tokens.js or factory-usage.js need to be aware of this convention difference to use the correct field names.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: lib/factory-accounts.js:121 uses accessToken/refreshToken from readAuthV2Files output. Compare to lib/codex-accounts.js:78 which uses access/refresh. readAuthV2Files in factory-crypto.js:171-172 maps snake_case to camelCase (accessToken, refreshToken).

sharedStateObservations.observation: findFactoryAccountByLabel and getAllFactoryLabels take an accounts array parameter, unlike the Codex equivalents (findAccountByLabel, getAllLabels) which internally call loadAllAccountsNoDedup(). This is a deliberate design from the feature spec resulting in a better-decoupled API, but the inconsistency between Codex and Factory patterns could confuse future workers.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: lib/factory-accounts.js:168 findFactoryAccountByLabel(accounts, label) vs lib/codex-accounts.js:147 findAccountByLabel(label) which internally loads accounts.

summary: The factory-accounts feature is well-implemented following the established codex-accounts.js pattern. All 9 required functions are present with proper JSDoc, error handling, and barrel re-exports. Tests are thorough with 51 cases covering all functions including error paths and edge cases. Three non-blocking issues noted: (1) lighter validation that omits token fields, (2) camelCase token naming differing from Codex convention, (3) single file path vs multi-path. All are reasonable design choices consistent with the feature spec. Two shared state observations about undocumented convention differences between Factory and Codex module patterns. PASS.
